generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, revising on purpose means planning around the topics you find hardest, perhaps research methods or a tricky theory, rather than the ones you enjoy. You test yourself to find the gaps, revise them actively, and pick a technique that fits, such as a mind map for linked models. Each round shows you what still needs work, so you adjust and go again.
generatedProse.worked-example: Priya is revising a psychology module with statistics, a set of key studies, and a theory with many linked parts. At first she plans to re-read everything for equal time. Instead she tests herself, finds statistics is her weakest area, and gives it the most time. She drills the key studies with flashcards, maps the linked theory, and works through statistics problems actively. By the exam she is strongest where she was once weakest.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, revising on purpose means running the three ideas together across the module. You plan around your weak topics, revise them actively, and choose a technique that fits each one, from flashcards for studies to maps for linked theory. Repeated and adjusted, that practice is what readies you for the exam.

check.body: A student lists her topics, tests herself to find the weak ones, gives them the most time, and revises each with a technique chosen to fit it. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: One revision practice at work: a strategy built on time and gaps, filled with active revision and techniques that fit the material.
_items.feedback: Yes. All three ideas are running together as one practice.

_items.text: That she is spending too long on revision and should cut it down.
